title: Sunday Chili
summary: American weekend ritual — low simmer while life happens elsewhere.
origins: Sunday pot cooking spans Irish stew, Italian gravy, and Southern church suppers. American chili fits the same slot: start mid-morning, feed a crowd by afternoon football. It is less a recipe than a calendar appointment with your Dutch oven.
history: Post-WWII suburban life cemented "Sunday dinner" as family anchor. Chili powder marketing (Gebhardt, Mexene) made Texas-style stew doable in Ohio kitchens by 1920. Game-day chili cook-offs became charity fundraisers nationwide from the 1970s onward.

timeline.event: Chili powder blends nationalize the flavor
Sunday family dinner peak in U.S. culture

teaching: Start early — chili improves with hours of gentle simmer.
Invite toppings bar: cheese, onion, jalapeño, Fritos — everyone builds their bowl.
Make double; freeze half. Future-you thinks you're a genius.
fun_fact: Sunday chili is a calendar appointment, not a recipe — the Dutch oven does the work while you watch the game.
